findings.name: a_quarter_of_the_suite_imports_the_entry_point
findings.note: Eleven of the forty upstream test files import from `src/index.ts` rather than from the module under test — `Signer` and `Matter` in one file, `Serder` and `versify` in another. Every symbol they reach is individually ported and VERIFIED; what is not is the entry point itself, whose §4.1 row is TODO because the curated re-export surface belongs to Roadmap 9.5. So the audit finds full behavioural coverage and one structural gap: this port has no equivalent of the single public surface a third of the suite imports through.
findings.consequence: Phase 9's exit gate requires every in-scope row VERIFIED, so 9.5 must close this row before release. Nothing behavioural is missing; a caller of this port reaches the same symbols through their own crates.

findings.name: one_application_module_is_still_split
findings.note: Ten of the forty test files reach `clienting.ts`, because it is where the client itself lives. Every capability behind it is VERIFIED — Roadmap 8.9 closed the last one, passcode rotation — but the row stays below VERIFIED because the curated endpoint-accessor surface is Roadmap 9.5's. It is the same gap as the entry point, seen from the other side: the behaviour is ported and the public shape is not yet settled.
findings.consequence: Also Roadmap 9.5's to close, and for the same reason. No unit case is left unanswered by it: every capability behind the row is VERIFIED with its own fixture and tests, and only the shape of the accessors this crate exposes is still open.
